$comment: The Blueprint page's sections, in render order.
This file is the spine: the page renders from it and every assertion reads it, so
'the page has these sections in this order' cannot drift from what is checked.
TIERS ARE PRESENTATION, NEVER PRESENCE. All of them render into the DOM in this
order, always. The tier decides prominence only:
1 = always visible.
2 = native <details>, default-collapsed. In the DOM, openable with JavaScript off.
This spine used to mirror the source PDF's sixteen sections, and the tests were
built to make dropping one impossible — the ordered-id assertion was designed to
go red the moment a section was deleted to make the page feel shorter.
That rule was doing its job and is deliberately superseded, not circumvented. The
page is no longer a sales page: it does not quote a price, it does not sell the
Blueprint, and it exists to establish credibility for a referral-led sales cycle.
Nine sections went with that decision — our-approach, who-it-is-for,
what-youll-receive, how-it-works, what-waiting-costs, the-offer, the-team, faq,
and the standalone hero, whose copy the route now owns directly.
Two were deliberately KEPT against the shorter design, because they carry every
claim in docs/blueprint-claims.json and every one of those claims traces to a
control in the framework: canadian-trust and our-commitments. Deleting them would
have removed the page's only verifiable content along with its sales copy. They
are tier 2 — present and traceable, not loud.
